{{short description|Belgian-American plant biologist}}
'''Maarten Chrispeels''' (born February 10, 1938) is a Belgian-American plant biologist and Distinguished Professor Emeritus at the [[University of California, San Diego]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Flesher |first=Jared |date=2009-04-30 |title=Sustainability and Crop Engineering |url=https://archive.nytimes.com/green.blogs.nytimes.com/2009/04/30/sustainability-and-crop-engineering/ |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=Green Blog |language=en}}</ref> He is known for his research on the [[biosynthesis]] of [[storage protein]]s in [[legume]] seeds and for the discovery of water channel proteins ([[aquaporin]]s) in plants.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Hageman Lecturer Maarten J. Chrispeels Colloquium: "The Use of Lectins and Enzyme Inhibitors For Genetic Engineering" |url=https://www.k-state.edu/bmb/about/seminars/hageman/1999-chrispeels.html |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=www.k-state.edu}}</ref> He was elected to the [[National Academy of Sciences|United States National Academy of Sciences]] in 1996.<ref name=":1">{{Cite web |last=Fikes |first=Bradley J. |date=2010-10-24 |title=SCIENCE: Scientist reinvents himself for second act |url=https://www.sandiegouniontribune.com/2010/10/24/science-scientist-reinvents-himself-for-second-act/ |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=[[San Diego Union-Tribune]] |language=en-US}}</ref> He is an inaugural fellow of [[American Society of Plant Biologists]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=McDonald |first=Kim |title=Professor Maarten Chrispeels Named an inaugural Fellow of the American Society of Plant Biologists |url=https://biology.ucsd.edu/about/news/article_091007.html |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=biology}}</ref> He was awarded [[Guggenheim Fellowship]]s in 1973.

== Early life and education ==
He was born in [[Kortenberg|Kortenberg, Belgium]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Chrispeels Laboratory |url=https://labs.biology.ucsd.edu/chrispeels/MJCcv.htm |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=labs.biology.ucsd.edu}}</ref> He studied at the Faculty of Agriculture in [[Ghent University|Ghent]], graduating summa cum laude.<ref>http://aix-slx.upol.cz/~fellner/doc/VORF-Lecture_4-2021.pdf

Maarten J. Chrispeels (1938) University of California San Diego Division of Biology</ref> In 1960, he moved to the United States to pursue a Ph.D. in Agronomy at the [[University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign|University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign]].<ref name=":2">https://aspb.org/wp-content/uploads/2020/03/Legacy-Society-Founding-Members-Maarten-Chrispeels.pdf

Maarten J. Chrispeels How did you spend your career?</ref> He completed postdoctoral research at [[Michigan State University]] and [[Purdue University]].<ref name=":0" />

== Career ==
In 1967, Chrispeels joined the newly established Department of Biology at [[University of California, San Diego|UCSD]], where he remained for over four decades.<ref name=":1" /> His early research focused on the secretion of [[hydroxyproline]]-rich [[glycoprotein]]s in [[plant cell]]s.<ref name=":3">{{Cite web |title=Plant cell biology research in the Chrispeels Laboratory: 1967-2005. |url=https://labs.biology.ucsd.edu/chrispeels/research06.htm#:~:text=The%20biosynthesis%20and%20secretion%20of,synthesis%20is%20turned%20down%20again. |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=labs.biology.ucsd.edu}}</ref> He later investigated the [[biosynthesis]] and vacuolar targeting of storage proteins in legume seeds, elucidating the role of the Golgi apparatus in protein trafficking.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Jiang |first1=Liwen |last2=Phillips |first2=Thomas E. |last3=Rogers |first3=Sally W. |last4=Rogers |first4=John C. |date=2000-08-21 |title=Biogenesis of the Protein Storage Vacuole Crystalloid |url=https://doi.org/10.1083/jcb.150.4.755 |journal=Journal of Cell Biology |volume=150 |issue=4 |pages=755–770 |doi=10.1083/jcb.150.4.755 |pmid=10953001 |pmc=2175284 |issn=0021-9525}}</ref> His work contributed to the understanding of how proteins are modified and transported within plant cells.<ref name=":1" />
Chrispeels' laboratory was among the first to use [[transgenic plants]] to study [[protein targeting]].<ref name=":3" /> While researching vacuolar transport signals, he and his colleagues identified [[aquaporin]]s, [[membrane protein]]s that facilitate water movement across [[cell membrane]]s, a discovery that advanced the field of plant-water relations.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Chrispeels |first1=Maarten J. |last2=Agre |first2=Peter |date=1994 |title=Aquaporins: water channel proteins of plant and animal cells |url=https://pure.johnshopkins.edu/en/publications/aquaporins-water-channel-proteins-of-plant-and-animal-cells-4 |journal=Trends in Biochemical Sciences |volume=19 |issue=10 |pages=421–425 |doi=10.1016/0968-0004(94)90091-4 |issn=0968-0004 |pmid=7529436}}</ref>

From 1996 to 2006, he served as director of the San Diego Center for Molecular Agriculture at UCSD.<ref name=":1" /> For 12 years (1999-2011) he served as an advisor to the [[President of Chile]] on the [[Millennium Science Initiative|Millennium Science Initiative Program]] and was elected as a foreign correspondent of the Academia Chilena de Ciencias.<ref>https://aspb.org/newsletter/archive/2016/NovDec16.pdf

Roll Up Your Sleeves! BY SALLY MACKENZIE University of Nebraska–Lincoln</ref>  He was awarded a Doctor Honoris Causa degree by the [[University of Guelph]], Canada.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Campus News: U of G to award honorary degrees, special awards at convocation |url=https://www.uoguelph.ca/news/archives/001202.html |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=www.uoguelph.ca}}</ref>

Chrispeels co-founded two [[biotechnology]] companies. Phylogix, aimed at developing radioprotective agents for stem cells, ceased operations following funding withdrawal.<ref name=":2" /> In 2010, he co-founded Arterra Bioscience with [[Gabriella Colucci]] in [[Italy]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-03-01 |title=A story of success, in Italy’s San Diego - Association des Étudiant·e·s en Ingénierie des Sciences du Vivant |url=https://aesv-epfl.ch/a-story-of-success-in-italys-san-diego/ |access-date=2025-06-02 |language=fr-FR}}</ref> The company focused on plant-based skincare products. After Arterra's IPO in 2021,<ref>{{Cite web |last=pix@pix.it |first=pix -- |title=Arterra Bioscience - about us |url=http://www.arterrabio.it/about-us.php |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170810054259/http://www.arterrabio.it/about-us.php |archive-date=2017-08-10 |access-date=2025-06-02 |website=www.arterrabio.it |language=en}}</ref> Chrispeels sold his shares and donated the proceeds to establish an endowed professorship in [[Botany|plant biology]] at [[University of California, San Diego|UCSD]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2012-03-08 |title=Janet Hageman Chrispeels Doctoral Fellowship in Educational Leadership Awardees |url=https://educationstudiesucsd.wordpress.com/2012/03/08/janet-hageman-chrispeels-doctoral-fellowship-in-educational-leadership-awardees/ |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=Department of Education Studies |language=en}}</ref>

== Research ==
In the 1980s, Chrispeels collaborated with researchers in Australia and the United States to develop insect-resistant [[transgenic crops]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Aguilera |first=Mario |title=Chrispeels Receives Gude Award from Plant Biology Society |url=https://biology.ucsd.edu/about/news/article_110119.html |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=biology.ucsd.edu}}</ref> His work on expressing a [[bean-derived]] [[alpha-amylase]] inhibitor in peas rendered them resistant to the [[pea bruchid beetle]], marking one of the earliest successful uses of genetic engineering for pest resistance in seeds.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Morton |first1=Roger L. |last2=Schroeder |first2=Hart E. |last3=Bateman |first3=Kaye S. |last4=Chrispeels |first4=Maarten J. |last5=Armstrong |first5=Eric |last6=Higgins |first6=Thomas J. V. |date=2000-04-11 |title=Bean α-amylase inhibitor 1 in transgenic peas ( Pisum sativum ) provides complete protection from pea weevil ( Bruchus pisorum ) under field conditions |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |language=en |volume=97 |issue=8 |pages=3820–3825 |doi=10.1073/pnas.070054597 |doi-access=free |issn=0027-8424 |pmc=18100 |pmid=10759552|bibcode=2000PNAS...97.3820M }}</ref>

Chrispeels has been an advocate for the use of [[biotechnology]] in addressing global food security and [[Sustainability|environmental sustainability]].<ref>{{Cite web |last=Archives |first=L. A. Times |date=2001-03-13 |title=Ecological Impact of GM Crops |url=https://www.latimes.com/archives/la-xpm-2001-mar-13-me-36865-story.html |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=Los Angeles Times |language=en-US}}</ref> He has emphasized the potential of [[genetically modified organism]]s (GMOs) to contribute to sustainable agriculture by enhancing [[crop yield]]s,<ref>{{Cite web |last=Cerier |first=Steven |date=2023-09-21 |title='Museum of Agriculture'? Could that be the fate of European farming if Greenpeace and other environmental activists succeed in blocking deregulation of crop gene editing? |url=https://geneticliteracyproject.org/2023/09/21/museum-of-agriculture-could-that-be-the-fate-of-european-farming-if-greenpeace-and-other-environmental-activists-succeed-in-blocking-deregulation-of-crop-gene-editing/ |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=Genetic Literacy Project |language=en-US}}</ref> improving resistance to pests and environmental stressors, and reducing the reliance on chemical inputs such as pesticides and [[herbicide]]s.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Wagner |first=David |date=2015-06-04 |title=San Diego Biotech Company: Don't Call Our Crop A GMO |url=https://www.kpbs.org/news/science-technology/2015/06/04/san-diego-biotech-company-dont-call-our-crop-gmo |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=KPBS Public Media |language=en}}</ref>

Chrispeels co-authored the textbook ''Plants, Genes and Crop Biotechnology'' and produced educational materials translated into multiple languages.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Plants, genes, and crop biotechnology / Maarten J. Chrispeels & David E. Sadava |url=https://www.si.edu/object/siris_sil_774060 |access-date=2025-05-27 |website=[[Smithsonian Institution]] |language=en}}</ref>
